Fuel & Tanks.text: The vessel’s fuel system lacked a shut-off valve at the tank outlet; the supply line was connected directly to the tank. Install a readily accessible shut-off valve at the tank outlet in compliance with Transport Canada Small Vessel Regulations and ABYC H-33, using a metallic or approved composite valve securely mounted and operable without tools.

The fuel tank was installed [insert location] and appeared serviceable with correct piping. Each fuel hose was secured with only one clamp. ABYC H-33.2.2.2 requires two corrosion-resistant clamps adjacent to each barb, and H-33.2.2.3 requires clamps to be readily inspectable and serviceable. Although this vessel predates the requirement and compliance is advisory, fit a second clamp to each fuel hose for improved safety and serviceability.

The fuel tank was located [insert location]. The installation lacked a readily accessible shut-off valve at the tank outlet, and hose terminations were secured with only one clamp. Although the vessel was built prior to the applicable Transport Canada and ABYC standards, current best practice calls for a shut-off valve at the tank outlet (where siphoning is possible) and double clamping consistent with ABYC H-33. Recommend installing a marine-rated quarter-turn shut-off valve operable without tools and upgrading hose terminations with two corrosion-resistant clamps on all fuel-fill and barbed connections.
